restatements.text: Prohibits county jails from holding individuals past their normal release time solely because of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.

findings.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
findings.mechanism: Decreases state and local participation in immigration enforcement by forbidding county jails from honoring federal detainer requests to hold individuals.

analysis.answer: Under current law, each county decides whether to honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure establishes a statewide rule prohibiting county jails from holding individuals beyond their normal release time solely based on a federal immigration detainer.

County jails that currently honor detainer requests will have to change their release procedures to comply with the ban. Federal immigration authorities may adapt by conducting more apprehensions in the community or outside of jails.

The text addresses the practice of local jails holding individuals for federal immigration enforcement. The mechanism reaches this by explicitly banning county jails from holding people past their release date solely on the basis of an immigration detainer.
The state government gains authority by preempting local policy. County sheriffs and local governments lose the discretion to cooperate with federal immigration detainers by holding individuals.
